responses.reply:
Good catch — the newly supplied internal policy is binding and directly contradicts the frozen v2 decision, so I'm reopening the spec rather than treating this as a routine continuation.

Before I touch it, I preserved the frozen v2 spec verbatim at `history/spec-v2-<timestamp>.md`. The original 30-day decision (D1) wasn't a mistake — it was a legitimate choice given what was known at the time — but it's now superseded because a binding policy caps identifiable-record retention at 7 days, and you've said you can't waive that policy even though you own the implementation.

That resolves the *ceiling*, but not the exact value: the policy sets a maximum of 7 days, it doesn't mandate using the full 7. So — do you want retention set to exactly 7 days (the maximum the policy allows), or a shorter period for extra margin (e.g., 5 days)? That number determines the updated requirement (R1) and the new day-boundary acceptance checks (currently day 29/31, analogous to day N-1/N+1 around whatever value you pick), plus the duration parameter passed into the existing purge implementation and its tests.

Readiness gate: the contradiction is resolved, R1 has a concrete observable acceptance criterion (day 6 present / day 8 purged), the purge implementation and tests already take a duration parameter so this is a value change not a redesign, and no blocking ambiguity remains.
